Substitute the expression for $g(x)$ into $f$:
$$fg(x) = f(2x + 1) = (2x + 1)^2 + 3$$

Take the positive square root (since $x > -\frac{1}{2} \implies 2x + 1 > 0$) and solve for $x$:
$$2x + 1 = \sqrt{y - 3} \implies 2x = \sqrt{y - 3} - 1 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{y - 3} - 1\right)$$
$$(fg)^{-1}(x) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{x - 3} - 1\right)$$

Determine the domain of $(fg)^{-1}$ from the range of $fg$:
$$\text{For } x > -\frac{1}{2}, \quad 2x + 1 > 0 \implies (2x + 1)^2 > 0 \implies fg(x) > 3$$
$$\text{Domain of } (fg)^{-1}: \quad x > 3$$

Write the explicit expressions for $fg(x) - 3$ and $gf(x)$:
$$fg(x) - 3 = \left( (2x + 1)^2 + 3 \right) - 3 = (2x + 1)^2 = 4x^2 + 4x + 1$$
$$gf(x) = 2(x^2 + 3) + 1 = 2x^2 + 6 + 1 = 2x^2 + 7$$

Equate both expressions and form a standard quadratic equation:
$$4x^2 + 4x + 1 = 2x^2 + 7 \implies 2x^2 + 4x - 6 = 0$$
$$\text{Divide by 2:} \quad x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for $x > 0$:
$$(x + 3)(x - 1) = 0 \implies x = 1 \quad (\text{rejecting } x = -3 < 0)$$
